chunks: And from it, regarding the description of the ascetics:

They were a people from among the people of this world but were not its people, so they were in it as though they did not belong to it. They acted in it based on what they perceived, and hastened in it to avoid what they feared. Their bodies moved among the people of the Hereafter. They see the people of this world attaching importance to the death of their bodies, while they themselves attach greater importance to the death of the hearts of those who are alive.

key_terms.الزُّهَّادِ: Ascetics / Those who practice renunciation of worldly desires

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual characteristic of ascetics regarding their relationship with this world and the Hereafter?
ai.summary: In Shia tradition, this passage from Nahj al-Balagha characterizes the *zuhhad* (ascetics) as those who maintain a state of *ghurrah* (spiritual vigilance), treating the world as a transient station rather than a permanent home. Sharif al-Radi highlights their unique duality: they engage in worldly duties with clarity of sight but prioritize the Hereafter, viewing the 'death of the heart'—spiritual heedlessness—as far more critical than physical demise. This reflects the Imami emphasis on balancing active participation in society with inner detachment, a concept deeply rooted in the teachings of Imam Ali.

en.sayed-ali-raza: [A part of the same sermon about ascetics :] They are from among the people of this world but are not its people, because they remain in it as though they do not belong to it. They act herein on what they observe and hasten here in (to avoid) what they fear. Their bodies move among the people of the next world. They see that the people of this world attach importance to the death of their bodies but they themselves attach more importance to the death of the hearts of those who are living.
